cultural.vision_reason: A woman's coat combining indigo cotton, ikat/atlas silk panels, and cross-stitch embroidery — materials and techniques consistent with Central Asian (Tajik/Uzbek) village dress; garment type fits the claimed ethnicity's traditional attire.

physical.title: coat (jillāyeh)
physical.summary: Village woman's short-sleeved coat (jillāyeh), made of indigo-dyed cotton with satin (ikat and atlas), taffeta and cotton appliqué patches along the front in various shades of red, yellow and green.  The coat also has panels of multi-coloured embroidery in a variety of stitches, including open-work and cross-stitch, along the sleeves as well as on the side and back skirt panels. The coat could be reversed and worn inside-out, the inner lapels embroidered in cross-stitch in shades of yellow, green, white, blue, black and red.  The coat has a yoke and under-arm inserts of red cotton and is trimmed along the neck-line with red satin and along the front opening with red cotton cord.
